properties.name: cap:graph-algorithms gets the check it already had — recorded partial, with the missing half named
properties.rationale:
THE RESOLUTION TURNED ON A DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING: a detector reporting absence of a RECORD is not the same as absence of a CHECK, and the two want opposite responses. Writing a new test to satisfy a recording gap would be the tail wagging the dog; recording a check that does not exist would be the forgery the gap exists to prevent. Measuring first is what told them apart — 47 passing cases and three verified consumers.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLOSE, and `covers: partial` is the mechanism that says so rather than a caveat in prose nobody reads. The tests are UPSTREAM's, absorbed with the code, and verify the algorithms in isolation. The capability claims something stronger — that reflow2 owns this theory — and three things remain unchecked: that the absorption preserved behaviour (`cap:certify-restructuring` was never run against it), that `paths.rs`/`error.rs` do anything (0 tests, and `paths` has no reflow2 call site at all), and that reflow2's own eight consumed entry points give right answers on design-shaped graphs.

📌 The honest close of those three is one test that drives the three consumers over a known design graph and asserts the structural answers. Recorded here rather than done, because it is an hour of real work and a different question from the one asked.

properties.summary: `unverified_capability` fired on `cap:graph-algorithms` at severity 0.55, the highest open gap. Measured before acting: 47 unit tests already exist inline in `graphalg/` and pass, and all three consumers (`structure.rs`, `allocate.rs`, `flow.rs`) carry their own passing checks. A RECORDING gap, not a coverage hole. Records `ver:graph-algorithms-unit-suite` (passing, run 2026-08-26) with `IMPLEMENTS covers: partial` from `art:graphalg`.
